requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
**Judgment:** `requirements.index.navigation` is met. The implementation is marked completely, and the tests cover its obligations and the `.md` boundary. **Implementation** - **Definition badges and "See evidence" links:** `replace_definitions` in `src/lib.rs` looks up the detail path in the `DetailPlan` via `detail_path`. When one exists, it renders the definition badge as ``. After each requirement or example body it emits `

See evidence

`. Without a plan it falls back to a `span`, which is right because no detail page exists then. The hrefs come from `chapter_href`. - **Anchored badge:** the badge id is `habeas--`, built from the same `DefinitionKind::anchor` that detail pages link to. `anchor` is marked `{impl}`. - **Detail pages link back:** `render_detail_page` in `src/index.rs` always emits `[View definition](chapter_href(detail_path, definition.path, #anchor))`. When `index_path` is `Some`, it also emits `[Requirements index](…)` before it. - **Reference badges:** `reference_badge` still links to `chapter_href(current, target.path, #anchor)`. It is marked as an implementation of `book_badges` rather than this requirement. `replace_inline_references` is marked `{impl}` for this requirement and calls it. The `book_badges` text covers "links to the badge at the corresponding definition", and `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` tests it. - **`.md` in names:** `chapter_href` ends with `href.replace(".md", "%2Emd")`, with a comment explaining why. It is used for definition badges, "See evidence" links, detail-to-definition links, detail-to-index links, index table rows, and reference badges. It is marked `{impl}`. - **Plumbing:** `DetailPlan::detail_path`, `is_detail_path` and `populate` (index table links and nested chapter creation) are all marked. - **Marking:** I found no navigation behaviour in unmarked code, and the marked code adds no behaviour beyond this requirement or other definitions it also implements. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (`src/lib.rs`) covers: - a requirement, a named example and a `cli.mdbook` requirement; - badge `href`s, each with `%2Emd` encoding; - exactly 3 "See evidence" links; - the "View definition" back-link, including the encoded `.md` anchor; - no "Requirements index" link when there is no index. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (`src/index.rs`) covers: - the badge `id`/`href` pair; - index table links; - the "Requirements index … · View definition" back-links from a nested path (`../../appendix/…`); - the cross-directory case. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` unit-tests `chapter_href` in both directions, for the detail link and the anchored definition link, with `requirements.cli.mdbook`. - Reference-badge linking is tested under `book_badges`, for example the nested-chapter test. **Residual gaps:** none significant. One small point: the `.md` boundary is tested at `chapter_href` and detail-page level, not separately for reference badges. They share `chapter_href`, so this is acceptable.
